reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, batch 3

samples_reviewed.question_text: What fraction does \(\frac{1}{8}\) equal parts represent?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Competency is 'Read and write unit fractions in fraction notation' but 2 of 5 samples ('Write 596 in words' -> 'five hundred ninety-six', 'Write 456 in words') are whole-number word-form tasks with no fraction, numerator, or denominator anywhere in the item.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The number_reading DNA (1 axis, 2 combos per variant_registry) is paired onto this node and appears to inject the off-topic 3-digit word-form items; the fractions DNA's 9 combos are the only ones actually relevant to 'fraction notation' here.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: 'Write 596 in words' demands multi-digit place-value-to-words conversion, a materially different and arguably harder skill than reading '1/8', so the two DNAs pull the item's cognitive target in inconsistent directions within one node.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The number_reading axis contributes zero variants that touch fraction notation, so roughly 40% of the registered variant space for this node (its 2 number_reading combos) cannot possibly serve the stated competency of reading/writing fractions.

competency_alignment.rationale: 'Write 456 in words' belongs to place-value/number-naming competencies from a different strand entirely, not to fraction notation, so the difficulty progression does not track the exact wording of this lc and instead drifts outside it.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The fraction denominator (8) is within the allowed range for this node group, but the whole numbers 456 and 596 injected by number_reading have no defined scale relationship to a unit-fraction competency at all, making 'appropriate range' unanswerable for that half.
